picks.headline: Mathematicians use AI to find mysterious symmetries, solving decades-old problem
picks.excerpt: By intertwining human insight with AI scale, mathematicians and amateurs found all 25,000 cases of one inverse Galois problem, collapsing a decades-old mystery posed at an American Institute of Mathematics AI sprint.
picks.rationale: A new, completed result, not the OpenAI Navier-Stokes story again: a human-plus-AI sprint closed all 25,000 cases of an inverse Galois problem. It is a working template for people and AI doing research together.

picks.headline: MIT's tiny flying robot gets 450% faster with AI
picks.excerpt: A new AI control system lets MIT's tiny flying robot move with insect-like agility, boosting its speed by about 450 percent and allowing it to pull off 10 somersaults in 11 seconds.
picks.rationale: AI is the whole story here: a learned controller gives a physical microrobot a 450% speed gain, with numbers that are easy to picture (10 somersaults in 11 s). It also adds robotics to a section that has been heavy on biology and math.

picks.headline: New LightTok chip converts light directly into 'tokens' for AI
picks.excerpt: Nanjing University's 2D 'LightTok' chip converts raw light directly into tokens that on-chip AI models can process, skipping energy-hungry analog-to-digital steps in vision sensors for drones and autonomous machines.
picks.rationale: A concrete new device, not a review. The sensor turns light straight into model tokens and skips the ADC step. This is a different story from the UCLA physical-AI review published 09-22, and its AI angle is stronger than the Phys.org nanostructures item.

picks.headline: AI assistant learns from radiology reports to spot problems in abdominal scans
picks.excerpt: An abdominal CT scan packs an extraordinary amount of information into a single image, layering dozens of organs and hundreds of possible conditions. It's widely considered one of the most complex scans in medicine to read, and even expert radiologists need time to carefully untangle what they're looking at. To help ease some of their workload, researchers presented a new AI assistant called RADAR
picks.rationale: The strongest clinical-AI pick in the pool. RADAR learns from existing radiology reports instead of hand labels to read one of medicine's hardest scans, so the model is central to the story. It was verified via RSS only, so the body needs an enrichment check.

picks.excerpt: During the production of fermented products such as kefir, Parmesan, or mountain cheese, as well as in the production of protein powders, bitter-tasting peptides can form, which impair the taste and thus the acceptability of the products.
